# Support Matrix

Which ROS 2 patterns rcllf converts, which it warns about and which it refuses. Each row is one feature. Read the Support column first: **Supported** converts, **Warns** converts and prints a diagnostic, **Rejected** stops generation with an error. The Evidence column says how far testing reaches (legend below). The Playground example column names a package under `packages/src` or `packages/src/fixtures` that shows the behavior; the first container start builds only the learning-path examples, so build the others with `docker compose run --rm -e ENTRYPOINT_PACKAGES=<package> dev` (see the [Docker reference](../reference/docker.md)). Diagnostic codes are explained in the [diagnostic code catalog](../reference/diagnostic-codes.md). The [Soundness Checker](soundness.md) checks the runtime half by tracing a real run and comparing it with the extracted model.

**Middleware.** rcllf requires Fast DDS (`rmw_fastrtps_cpp`, the RMW the container sets): the binding keys every received sample by its publisher GID and publication sequence number, and a program with an admitted correspondence edge refuses any other RMW at startup. Cyclone DDS does not report the publication sequence number. Zenoh (`rmw_zenoh_cpp`) is untested.

**Deployment.** Every node of a launch file in one process, and one process per node (`--federate per-node`) under centralized coordination, are supported. Per-process partitions, a custom federation YAML, federation across hosts and decentralized coordination are experimental; see [Federation](federation.md).

**Evidence** says how the claim was tested:

- **validated**: exercised by a system whose evaluation runs report the feature as supported (complete, covered and reconciled traces). The evaluation systems and their run data are described in the rcllf paper and are not part of this repository.
- **experimental**: analyzed and generated by the playground, with no evaluation row behind it. Some of these examples also run in the CI runtime smoke tests.
- **refused**: generation refuses the input with an error diagnostic.
- **unresolved**: the analyser reports it, and the runtime behavior is not determined by the generated program (a warning or an unresolved value).

## Stated limits

These are the stated limits L1 to L8. Each one bounds the features that cite it in the Limits column.

| Limit | Statement |
|---|---|
| <a id="l1"></a>L1 | Detected loss holds within one process. An admitted cross-federate edge between two federates on one host detects loss too (shown in the evaluation of the rcllf paper). A relay publisher is admitted too. Federates on two hosts are admitted when the deployment declares a bound on the offset of the two clocks below the edge timeout. Cross-federate edges that are not admitted stay undetected. A decentralized edge is admitted too, except into a BNA input. A cross-federate link has `after 0` by default and is admitted at every `after` of 0 or more, because the sender sends at the publishing tag. The generation switch that chose `after 0` is gone. Only the flush sender, used under decentralized coordination or with `RCLLF_XFED_FLUSH=1`, still refuses an `after` of 1 ns (`xfed_flush_min`). An earlier version refused every flush edge (`xfed_flush_no_complete`), because the flush carried no COMPLETE record. The flush message carries one COMPLETE number per time, a lost flush message is reported as CONTROL_FAILURE, and flush edges, among them a decentralized edge with an `after` above 0, are admitted again. Federates on two hosts without a declared bound are refused at the first record. A legacy cross-federate link written at a third microstep of one time exits instead of merging. Under decentralized coordination such a link exits at its second microstep of one time, since the receiver judges that second message tardy and moves or drops it. A cross-federate edge detects a lost sample at S(a), the physical start of the publishing activation on the publisher's clock, plus d plus its own timeout. A sample counts only by its ingress stamp, and every publication of one activation shares the cutoff S(a) + d + T, so a publish delayed by an upstream join keeps its full d + T and no timeout is chained over the publisher's inputs. The timeout chain, its loop slack rule and the join hold limit are gone. A lost sample's join still holds its tag until its cutoff, since LF runs the reactions of a tag level by level, which costs latency but no spurious loss. A subscription can set `join: deferred`: its drain runs at the cutoff tag, publish tag + d + T, a deferred edge never blocks the LF worker waiting for its sample, and its dispatch tag is fixed. Only a sample taken in strictly before the cutoff is delivered there, and the eligible input set can still differ across runs when an arrival races the cutoff. Blocking stays the default, and LF still waits for physical time to reach each tag. An edge inside one federate has no cutoff: the publishing thread takes the sample from the subscriber's in-process reader before the publish returns, a sample not found there ends `LOST` (`local_undelivered`, a reconcile failure), the drain never waits, and `join: deferred` on such an edge is a generation error. A cross-federate cutoff counts from the publication tag instead of S(a), t + max(0, d) + T + eps, so a sender behind its tags makes its outputs late at the receiver, and the `publisher_late` counter is gone. |
| <a id="l2"></a>L2 | Running Nav2 under lfc is future work. Gazebo `/clock` against logical time is not supported. A tf2 lookup is supported only through `rcllf_tf2::AcquisitionLookup`, which decides each request by the logical deadline request tag + wait bound, with a `TransformListener` whose `/tf` and `/tf_static` are published by nodes of the system; a direct or blocking `Buffer` lookup and `/tf` from outside the system are refused with RCLLF-R002. Action servers are supported when they send feedback and results only from callbacks that LF reactions run. A server that sends from its own thread is refused with RCLLF-H011. A server whose only clients are outside the LF system runs at tags set by request arrival. Client feedback is not a correspondence edge. An action with several client nodes, and two actions on one node where one name is a path suffix of the other (`move` and `/right/move`), are refused at generation. A server whose action also has a client inside the LF system takes no goal from a client outside it. For a lifecycle node, a transition made at tag T holds for every reaction after T, an inactive node runs no callback, its entities are re-bound after each change, and a handle a node drops at tag T stays valid for the other reactions at T. A `LifecyclePublisher` holds its activation for the tag as well, so a publish by another reaction at T does not depend on the reaction order. A transition a reaction makes holds from the same tag in every run. A transition completed outside LF, including `ros2 lifecycle set`, enters LF as a physical action and holds from the tag after that action, which follows the wall clock and so differs between runs. A node built without the lifecycle communication interface, or an executable without the binding's publication gate, falls back to reading the state when a callback returns or at a boundary, so such a transition carries no timestamp and can apply at a logical tag earlier than its physical time. A topic edge of a lifecycle node is admitted to correspondence, also across federates, and a publisher the node makes after startup is bound to the edge. A subscription that a lifecycle hook makes or resets keeps its edge legacy, which L6 bounds. A node that leaves the active state has the pending requests of its service clients pruned and the goals of its action clients cancelled at the first tag after the deactivation, so a reactivated node starts with none. This holds for a client type the analysis names in full (`pkg::srv::Name`, `pkg::action::Name`). A client of another type keeps its work in flight, and the binding warns once. |
| <a id="l3"></a>L3 | A self-loop edge that correspondence admission refuses stays on the stub path without a logical delivery guarantee. The reasons include `self_loop_split`, a subscription in another callback group than its publishers, and `burst_unbounded`, a publisher without analyzed publish bounds. RCLLF-H001 and RCLLF-H002 are also checked at startup on the effective QoS of the reader of every admitted and legacy edge. Every other subscription, such as an input from outside the analyzed graph, gets RCLLF-H001 at startup by its own reaction, so twin subscriptions on one topic are judged apart, and a subscription whose reliability the analysis did not see logs RCLLF-H000 with the effective value. A publisher whose reliability the analysis did not see logs RCLLF-H000 at startup with the effective value too. Two kinds of publisher are not checked at startup and keep only the static RCLLF-H000. One is a publisher whose topic is computed at run time. The other is a user publisher with the message type of a publisher the node creates for itself on the same topic, which is `/rosout`, `/parameter_events`, the `transition_event` topic of a lifecycle node, and the `_action/feedback` and `_action/status` topics of an action server. |
| <a id="l4"></a>L4 | The reference-system evaluation of the rcllf paper (its data is not part of this repository) reports 5 of 160 runs as failed, all `stock-launch-per-node-depth8` (3 idle, 2 under `cpu-mem`), carrying 6 counted losses (an earlier evaluation: 12 runs, 15 losses, same class). The per-reader accounting puts each counted loss inside the match-resolution window, a gap between match-probe polls. They are reported, not rerun. That only depth 8 fails is an artefact of the classifier: a depth-1 reader counted the same startup losses as overwritten. With the fix, a 20-run stock depth-1 control fails 4 runs, so the stock depth-1 rows await a re-summary. CPU is whole-tree rusage. The trace column is callback wall time, and the host had no kernel traces. |
| <a id="l5"></a>L5 | The rcllf row of the loss evaluation is "detected loss under sustained overload", not a determinism row. The per-ID gate detects every missing ID. With `take_timeout_ms` 5000 every ID is delivered, at a latency cost. |
| <a id="l6"></a>L6 | A legacy edge carries only a trigger, and the subscriber takes whatever sample its reader holds when the reaction runs. Its value at a tag therefore depends on the wall-clock arrival of samples. A receiver that runs behind the sender in wall time can take a later sample at an earlier tag, and a sender that runs behind the receiver can leave an earlier sample in the reader. Every topic edge that correspondence admission refuses with a reason is such an edge, for example `transient_local`, a fan-in group whose members' delays differ (`fan_in_release_mismatch`) or `burst_unbounded`. Samples are not filtered by stamp. |
| <a id="l7"></a>L7 | Several publishing nodes into one subscription are delivered in one order: by release tag, then by the rank of the publisher's LF instance name, then in publication order . A fan-in group is admitted or stays legacy as a whole. It stays legacy, every member with a trigger-only edge, when a member is refused for any reason (for example `transient_local` or `burst_unbounded`), when the members' delays differ (`fan_in_release_mismatch`, for a deferred group also their chained timeouts), when some members cross federates and others do not (`fan_in_mixed_locality`), when a member's publisher is the subscribing node (`fan_in_self_loop`), when a member rebinds with a lifecycle node (`fan_in_rebind`) or when one node publishes the topic from two publisher objects (`fan_in_shared_publisher`). A group into a BoundedNearestToAnchor input is refused (`fan_in_bna_input`) and generation stops with `RCLLF-H003`. A lost sample holds the group's drain until its cutoff, so the later samples of the other publishers wait behind it in physical time, at unchanged tags. A writer outside the analyzed graph, such as `ros2 topic pub`, is never delivered (`UNRESOLVED`). Under decentralized coordination the order holds only while every record arrives within its STP window, and a tardy record's missing dispatch can count as an order violation that ends the run with exit code 3. Known limitation: this case has no experiment. |
| <a id="l8"></a>L8 | A two-input `message_filters` ExactTime or ApproximateTime synchronizer is claimed on the domain `mf-sync/1` only: both inputs are admitted correspondence edges with one link delay, at most the declared burst per tag, and `message_filters` 4.11.17 with `rclcpp` 28.1.22. On it the converted synchronizer emits the same signal and drop stream as the stock header run off-line on the LF arrival order (tick, then input 0 before input 1, then publish order), which is not the arrival order of a stock ROS run, so the claim is "matches message_filters 4.11.17 for the LF arrival order", never "equivalent to stock ROS". An input that is a legacy edge, including an input from outside the analyzed graph (`external`), refuses generation with `RCLLF-H003 sync_input_legacy:<reason>`, unequal input delays with `sync_input_delay_unequal`. A lost or overflowing sample is reported `out_of_domain`, not compared. Rate bounds (`setInterMessageLowerBound`, `setMaxIntervalDuration`), three or more inputs and `LatestTime` stay refused. |
